name: -ever words: whatever, whoever, wherever
subtitle: Add -ever to a question word when it doesn't matter which, who or where: Whatever you choose is fine. Wherever she goes, she takes a book. However hard I try, I can't open it.

flow.text: what / who / which / where / when / how
= it doesn't matter which / who / where …

concept.exampleHtml: Whatever you cook, I'll eat it. — Wherever she goes, she takes her camera.

qa.html: -ever means: it doesn't matter. Whatever you choose is fine. (= It doesn't matter what you choose.) It can also mean any … that: Take whatever you need. (= anything that you need)

The words: whatever, whoever, whichever, wherever, whenever, however. Use whichever when there is a small choice: Take whichever coat you like. (There are only a few coats.) Use whatever when the choice is open.

An -ever word starts a clause with its own subject and verb. Whoever finishes first wins. / I'll go wherever you go. / Whenever I'm tired, I make tea. For the future, use the present simple: Whatever happens, we'll stay.

however + adjective or adverb means no matter how: However hard I try, I can't do it. However late it is, call me. The adjective comes straight after however. Do not mix this up with the linker However, … (= but): The room was small. However, it was cheap.

No matter + question word says the same: No matter what you say = Whatever you say. No matter how hard I try = However hard I try. But a clause that is the subject or object needs the -ever word: Whatever you choose is fine.

Typical mistakes: ✗ However I try hard, I fail. → ✓ However hard I try, I fail. · ✗ Whatever will happen, we'll stay. → ✓ Whatever happens, we'll stay. (no will) · ✗ Whatever you choose, is fine. → ✓ Whatever you choose is fine. (no comma between subject and verb)

concept.noteHtml: -ever clauses are close to relative clauses: Take whatever you need = Take everything that you need. For relative clauses, see Relative clauses and Non-defining relative clauses. For the present simple with a future meaning, see Time clauses. On its own, Whatever. can sound bored or rude: it means I don't care. Use it carefully.

exercises.title: Which word fits?
exercises.hint: Think about what the -ever word replaces: a thing, a person, a place, a time, one of a few, or a way.
exercises.hintHtml: whatever · whoeverany thing · any personwherever · wheneverany place · any timewhicheverone of a small choicehowever + adjectiveno matter how …

items.prompt: You can sit ___ you like, because the cinema is empty.
items.why: You can sit in any place: wherever.

items.prompt: Take ___ you need from the fridge: milk, eggs or cheese.
items.why: Milk, eggs and cheese are things: whatever (= anything that you need).

items.prompt: There are three coats here. Take ___ one you like.
items.why: The choice is small (three coats), so we use whichever.

items.prompt: Call me ___ you need help, day or night.
items.why: Day or night means at any time: whenever.
A person finishes and gets a prize: whoever.

items.prompt: ___ hard I study, I always forget the dates.
items.why: However goes directly before an adjective: however hard (= no matter how hard).

items.prompt: No matter ___ she says, he never listens.
items.why: After no matter we use the plain question word: no matter what, not no matter whatever.

exercises.title: Say it another way.
exercises.hint: Tap the sentence with -ever, then the sentence with no matter that means the same.
